So I listen to a gaming podcast quite a bit, and these are my thoughts on this: I think that one of the contributors is both misguided, and that what he said is being blown out of proportion. Ok, so first off, this contributor is a video guy. Essentially, he's the one who sets up the cameras for the podcast videos, captures gameplay videos (I know. Ironic), and films a lot of their other video segments. I truly believe that he's only ever on the show when they have no one else to use. Around the time of this podcast, the show consisted of a few main hosts, and when one of them couldn't be on it, he would come in. So yeah, he's the guy who they say "we need someone else in here..."

But on to context: if I remember correctly, they were talking about PCs vs consoles, and how there's a theory that a certain console brand is just going to turn into an upgradable type product, where you just upgrade parts every couple of years. This contributor is not a fan of this, and was giving reasons why he likes consoles over PCs. From the context of the conversation, what it sounded like he was trying to say was that he preferred the "ready out of the box" quality of consoles over PCs, and part of that "ready out of the box" includes a piece of hardware that, out of the box, gives you the ability to record gameplay. So yes, what he was saying was incorrect, but it's one of those cases of "I see what you were going for."

Anyway, I enjoy the podcasts from this gaming media outlet. Yes, they absolutely say things that I disagree with, but at the end of the day, they're entertaining to listen to. A new contributor just joined their show recently and I actually really enjoy hearing what she has to say. She's called out the misguided contributor on his mistakes multiple times, and it's SO satisfying!
